description: Use this when the user wants a calendar file, for example "make a calendar file for this meeting", "create an .ics for my weekly class", "export these dates so I can import them". Pass 1 to 50 events, each with a title, a start (a date for an all-day event, or a date and time) and an end or duration_minutes, plus a timezone (IANA name such as America/New_York) for a time without Z or an offset. Optional per event: location, description, reminder_minutes and a repeat (freq daily, weekly, monthly or yearly with interval, until or count, and byday for weekly). Returns the .ics text, a download link that works for 24 hours, its expiry and the event count. It makes a file only; it does not add anything to a calendar.

duration_minutes.description: Length of a timed event instead of end.

end.description: Same format as start. For an all-day event it is the last day, inclusive. Give this or duration_minutes.

byday.description: Weekdays for a weekly repeat, e.g. ["MO","WE"].

count.description: Number of occurrences. Give until or count.

interval.description: Every N days, weeks, months or years. Default 1.

reminder_minutes.description: Show a reminder this many minutes before the event.

start.description: 2026-11-02 for an all-day event, or 2026-11-02T09:30 (add Z or an offset such as +07:00 if there is no timezone).

timezone.description: IANA time zone name such as America/New_York. Required for a time without Z or an offset.

filename.description: File name, letters and digits; .ics is added.

name: make_calendar_file

download_url.description: Link that works for 24 hours, or null when no link could be made.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working (ISO 8601 UTC).

message.description: What to fix in the input when status is invalid.

title: Make a calendar (.ics) file
